1:1.sourceText: Τὸν μὲν πρῶτον λόγον ἐποιησάμην περὶ πάντων, ὦ Θεόφιλε, ὧν ἤρξατο ὁ Ἰησοῦς ποιεῖν τε καὶ διδάσκειν,
1:1.targetText: The former account, indeed, I made concerning all things, O Theophilus, that Jesus began both to do and to teach,

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with Jesus.

1:2.sourceText: ἄχρι ἧς ἡμέρας ἐντειλάμενος τοῖς ἀποστόλοις διὰ Πνεύματος Ἁγίου οὓς ἐξελέξατο ἀνελήμφθη·
1:2.targetText: until the day in which, having given command through the Holy Spirit to the apostles whom He chose out, He was taken up,

groups.note: Actual genitive relative/day construction gives the temporal day on which the taking-up occurred. English in which expresses that relative-time relation without a separate Greek in preposition.

1:3.sourceText: οἷς καὶ παρέστησεν ἑαυτὸν ζῶντα μετὰ τὸ παθεῖν αὐτὸν ἐν πολλοῖς τεκμηρίοις, δι’ ἡμερῶν τεσσεράκοντα ὀπτανόμενος αὐτοῖς καὶ λέγων τὰ περὶ τῆς βασιλείας τοῦ Θεοῦ·
1:3.targetText: to whom He also presented Himself alive after His suffering, in many certain proofs, being seen by them through forty days, and speaking the things concerning the Kingdom of God.

groups.note: Actual accusative αὐτόν is the personal subject of the suffering infinitive. English His recasts that same subject as the possessive of suffering; no genitive Greek pronoun is substituted.
Actual ὀπτανόμενος is the present appearing/being-visible participle, rendered being seen; the original participial form and appearance head remain.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed in the English His-suffering nominal phrase.

1:4.sourceText: καὶ συναλιζόμενος παρήγγειλεν αὐτοῖς ἀπὸ Ἱεροσολύμων μὴ χωρίζεσθαι, ἀλλὰ περιμένειν τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν τοῦ Πατρὸς ἣν ἠκούσατέ μου·
1:4.targetText: And being assembled together with them, He commanded them not to depart from Jerusalem, but to wait for the promise of the Father, “Which you heard from Me;

groups.note: LSV uses the assembled-together sense of συναλίζομαι. The primary lexical entry also records the eating-with sense; both concern this printed verb, not different source words. See https://www.billmounce.com/greek-dictionary/synalizo .

The actual dative αὐτοῖς names the command recipients and the same people present in the immediately preceding assembled-with participle. English states with them and commanded them; both local roles retain one real source personal identity, without a second written pronoun.

1:5.sourceText: ὅτι Ἰωάνης μὲν ἐβάπτισεν ὕδατι, ὑμεῖς δὲ ἐν Πνεύματι βαπτισθήσεσθε Ἁγίῳ οὐ μετὰ πολλὰς ταύτας ἡμέρας.
1:5.targetText: because John, indeed, immersed in water, but you will be immersed in the Holy Spirit not many days after these.”

groups.note: The actual dative water expresses the immersion medium, rendered in water without an independently printed Greek in preposition at that first phrase.

1:6.sourceText: Οἱ μὲν οὖν συνελθόντες ἠρώτων αὐτὸν λέγοντες Κύριε, εἰ ἐν τῷ χρόνῳ τούτῳ ἀποκαθιστάνεις τὴν βασιλείαν τῷ Ἰσραήλ;
1:6.targetText: They, therefore, indeed, having come together, were questioning Him, saying, “Lord, do You at this time restore the kingdom to Israel?”

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with this time.
Actual εἰ marks the polar whether question. English forms the direct do-You-restore question without a separate whether/if word.

1:7.sourceText: εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς Οὐχ ὑμῶν ἐστιν γνῶναι χρόνους ἢ καιροὺς οὓς ὁ Πατὴρ ἔθετο ἐν τῇ ἰδίᾳ ἐξουσίᾳ,
1:7.targetText: And He said to them, “It is not yours to know times or seasons that the Father appointed in His own authority;

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with His own authority.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV includes an opening connective, corroborated by the longer TR δέ wording. Pinned N1904 begins directly with said without that separate connective.

1:8.sourceText: ἀλλὰ λήμψεσθε δύναμιν ἐπελθόντος τοῦ Ἁγίου Πνεύματος ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς, καὶ ἔσεσθέ μου μάρτυρες ἔν τε Ἱερουσαλὴμ καὶ ἐν πάσῃ τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ καὶ Σαμαρίᾳ καὶ ἕως ἐσχάτου τῆς γῆς.
1:8.targetText: but you will receive power at the coming of the Holy Spirit on you, and you will be witnesses for Me both in Jerusalem, and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the end of the earth.”

groups.note: The actual aorist coming-upon participle forms the Spirit genitive-absolute time circumstance. English at the coming nominalizes that temporal predicate without a separately written at preposition or coming noun.

Actual μου is genitive my, qualifying witnesses. LSV for Me corresponds to the same named speaker under the TR dative μοι reading. The actual genitive source form remains explicit rather than being relabeled dative.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with all Judea.

1:9.sourceText: καὶ ταῦτα εἰπὼν βλεπόντων αὐτῶν ἐπήρθη, καὶ νεφέλη ὑπέλαβεν αὐτὸν ἀπὸ τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν αὐτῶν.
1:9.targetText: And having said these things—they beholding—He was taken up, and a cloud received Him up from their sight;

groups.note: Actual ὀφθαλμῶν is the plural eyes noun, rendered sight for the seeing faculty. The original eye head and plural form remain rather than a separately printed Greek sight noun.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with their sight.

1:10.sourceText: καὶ ὡς ἀτενίζοντες ἦσαν εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν πορευομένου αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἰδοὺ ἄνδρες δύο παρειστήκεισαν αὐτοῖς ἐν ἐσθήσεσι λευκαῖς,
1:10.targetText: and as they were looking steadfastly to the sky in His going on, then, behold, two men stood by them in white clothing,

groups.note: Actual genitive going participle with its personal subject supplies the temporal in-His-going-on phrase. English in makes that genitive-absolute time relation explicit without a separate Greek in word here.
Actual αὐτοῦ is the genitive subject of going, rendered His with the nominalized English going phrase; the same personal source identity is retained.
Actual καί connects the following behold scene, rendered then. No separate Greek τότε time adverb is printed at this position.

1:11.sourceText: οἳ καὶ εἶπαν Ἄνδρες Γαλιλαῖοι, τί ἑστήκατε βλέποντες εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν; οὗτος ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὁ ἀναλημφθεὶς ἀφ’ ὑμῶν εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν οὕτως ἐλεύσεται ὃν τρόπον ἐθεάσασθε αὐτὸν πορευόμενον εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν.
1:11.targetText: who also said, “Men, Galileans, why do you stand gazing into the sky? This Jesus who was received up from you into Heaven, will so come in what manner you saw Him going on to Heaven.”

groups.note: Actual ἑστήκατε is perfect active have-taken-your-stand, rendered present-state do you stand; the printed perfect remains.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek articles are not separately expressed with this Jesus or the two English Heaven designations.

1:12.sourceText: Τότε ὑπέστρεψαν εἰς Ἱερουσαλὴμ ἀπὸ ὄρους τοῦ καλουμένου Ἐλαιῶνος, ὅ ἐστιν ἐγγὺς Ἱερουσαλὴμ σαββάτου ἔχον ὁδόν.
1:12.targetText: Then they returned to Jerusalem from [that] called the Mount of Olives, that is near Jerusalem, a Sabbath’s journey;

groups.note: Actual Ἐλαιῶνος names the olive-grove/Olivet mountain, rendered of Olives with the actual Mount noun. It retains the place designation rather than an independently printed plural olive-tree noun. See https://www.billmounce.com/greek-dictionary/gk:1779 .

unmappedSource.reason: Actual ἔχον having introduces the measured journey distance. English states the Sabbath’s-journey distance nominally without a separate have predicate.

1:13.sourceText: καὶ ὅτε εἰσῆλθον, εἰς τὸ ὑπερῷον ἀνέβησαν οὗ ἦσαν καταμένοντες, ὅ τε Πέτρος καὶ Ἰωάνης καὶ Ἰάκωβος καὶ Ἀνδρέας, Φίλιππος καὶ Θωμᾶς, Βαρθολομαῖος καὶ Μαθθαῖος, Ἰάκωβος Ἀλφαίου καὶ Σίμων ὁ Ζηλωτὴς καὶ Ἰούδας Ἰακώβου.
1:13.targetText: and when they came in, they went up into the upper room, where were abiding both Peter, and James, and John, and Andrew, Philip, and Thomas, Bartholomew, and Matthew, James, of Alphaeus, and Simon the Zealot, and Judas, of James;

groups.note: The source names John then James in this first pair, while LSV names James then John. Each name and its immediate coordinating conjunction retain the actual named person rather than being paired by order.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed before both Peter in the personal list.

1:14.sourceText: οὗτοι πάντες ἦσαν προσκαρτεροῦντες ὁμοθυμαδὸν τῇ προσευχῇ σὺν γυναιξὶν καὶ Μαριὰμ τῇ μητρὶ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ καὶ σὺν τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς αὐτοῦ.
1:14.targetText: these were all continuing with one accord in prayer and supplication, with women, and Mary the mother of Jesus, and with His brothers.

groups.note: The actual dative article/prayer constituent supplies in prayer as the activity of continuing; no standalone Greek in preposition is printed.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with His brothers.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV includes an additional prayer/supplication noun and conjunction. Pinned N1904 has the one prayer noun without this added phrase.

1:15.sourceText: Καὶ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ταύταις ἀναστὰς Πέτρος ἐν μέσῳ τῶν ἀδελφῶν εἶπεν· ἦν τε ὄχλος ὀνομάτων ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ ὡσεὶ ἑκατὸν εἴκοσι
1:15.targetText: And in these days, Peter having risen up in the midst of the disciples, said (also the multitude of the names at the same place was, as it were, one hundred and twenty),

groups.note: Actual ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό is the same-place/together phrase, rendered at the same place. Place makes its adverbial location relation explicit without a written Greek place noun.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with these days.
Pinned N1904 names the brothers in the gathering. LSV follows the TR disciples wording, a different Greek μαθηταί head rather than the actual ἀδελφοί brother noun.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV names disciples in the gathering, corroborated by TR τῶν μαθητῶν. N1904 instead prints τῶν ἀδελφῶν, the brothers; the different lexical heads remain explicit.

1:16.sourceText: Ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί, ἔδει πληρωθῆναι τὴν γραφὴν ἣν προεῖπεν τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ Ἅγιον διὰ στόματος Δαυεὶδ περὶ Ἰούδα τοῦ γενομένου ὁδηγοῦ τοῖς συλλαβοῦσιν Ἰησοῦν,
1:16.targetText: “Men, brothers, it was necessary [for] this Writing to be fulfilled that the Holy Spirit spoke beforehand through the mouth of David, concerning Judas, who became guide to those who took Jesus,

groups.note: The actual accusative article/Writing phrase is the subject of the fulfilment infinitive under necessary. English [for] introduces that same infinitive subject; no separate Greek for preposition is printed.

unmappedSource.reason: The repeated Greek attributive article before Holy is not separately expressed in English.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV includes the demonstrative this, corroborated by the TR ταύτην reading. Pinned N1904 has the definite Writing without an independently written demonstrative here.

1:17.sourceText: ὅτι κατηριθμημένος ἦν ἐν ἡμῖν καὶ ἔλαχεν τὸν κλῆρον τῆς διακονίας ταύτης.
1:17.targetText: because he was numbered among us, and received the share in this ministry.

groups.note: The actual genitive article/ministry phrase qualifies the lot/share. English in this ministry recasts the same share relation; the source remains a genitive constituent rather than a Greek in preposition.

1:18.sourceText: οὗτος μὲν οὖν ἐκτήσατο χωρίον ἐκ μισθοῦ τῆς ἀδικίας, καὶ πρηνὴς γενόμενος ἐλάκησεν μέσος, καὶ ἐξεχύθη πάντα τὰ σπλάγχνα αὐτοῦ·
1:18.targetText: (This one, indeed, then, purchased a field out of the reward of unrighteousness, and falling headlong, burst apart in the midst, and all his bowels gushed forth,

groups.note: Actual πρηνὴς γενόμενος is the becoming-headlong/prone constituent, rendered falling headlong. The actual becoming verb and posture adjective remain rather than an independently printed πίπτω falling verb.

Actual ἐξεχύθη is aorist passive singular was-poured-out with the neuter-plural bowels subject. English gushed forth uses an active-style plural-subject expression; the original passive/singular form remains.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with his bowels.

1:19.sourceText: καὶ γνωστὸν ἐγένετο πᾶσι τοῖς κατοικοῦσιν Ἱερουσαλήμ, ὥστε κληθῆναι τὸ χωρίον ἐκεῖνο τῇ ἰδίᾳ διαλέκτῳ αὐτῶν Ἀκελδαμάχ, τοῦτ’ ἔστιν Χωρίον αἵματος.
1:19.targetText: and it became known to all those dwelling in Jerusalem, insomuch that this place is called, in their proper dialect, Aceldama, that is, Field of Blood.)

groups.note: The actual dative article/dialect constituent supplies in ... dialect as the language-of-naming relation; no standalone Greek in preposition is printed here.
Actual Ἀκελδαμάχ and English Aceldama designate the same named field with conventional spelling/transliteration variation; the written Greek ending is not overwritten.
Actual ἐκεῖνο is the distal that-place demonstrative; LSV renders this place in its restatement. The printed distal form remains explicit.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with this place.

1:20.sourceText: γέγραπται γὰρ ἐν βίβλῳ Ψαλμῶν Γενηθήτω ἡ ἔπαυλις αὐτοῦ ἔρημος καὶ μὴ ἔστω ὁ κατοικῶν ἐν αὐτῇ, καί Τὴν ἐπισκοπὴν αὐτοῦ λαβέτω ἕτερος.
1:20.targetText: For it has been written in [the] Scroll of Psalms: Let his lodging-place become desolate, and let no one be dwelling in it, and let another take his oversight.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek articles are not separately expressed with his lodging-place or his oversight.

1:21.sourceText: δεῖ οὖν τῶν συνελθόντων ἡμῖν ἀνδρῶν ἐν παντὶ χρόνῳ ᾧ εἰσῆλθεν καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ἐφ’ ἡμᾶς ὁ Κύριος Ἰησοῦς,
1:21.targetText: It is necessary, therefore, of the men who went with us during all the time in which the Lord Jesus went in and went out among us,

groups.note: Actual συνελθόντων is the aorist accompanying/coming-with participle qualifying the men. English makes that substantive modifier a who-went clause, preserving its real participial source form.

1:22.sourceText: ἀρξάμενος ἀπὸ τοῦ βαπτίσματος Ἰωάνου ἕως τῆς ἡμέρας ἧς ἀνελήμφθη ἀφ’ ἡμῶν, μάρτυρα τῆς ἀναστάσεως αὐτοῦ σὺν ἡμῖν γενέσθαι ἕνα τούτων.
1:22.targetText: beginning from the immersion of John, to the day in which He was received up from us, one of these to become with us a witness of His resurrection.”

1:23.sourceText: Καὶ ἔστησαν δύο, Ἰωσὴφ τὸν καλούμενον Βαρσαββᾶν, ὃς ἐπεκλήθη Ἰοῦστος, καὶ Μαθθίαν.
1:23.targetText: And they set two, Joseph called Barsabas, who was surnamed Justus, and Matthias,

1:24.sourceText: καὶ προσευξάμενοι εἶπαν Σὺ Κύριε καρδιογνῶστα πάντων, ἀνάδειξον ὃν ἐξελέξω ἐκ τούτων τῶν δύο ἕνα
1:24.targetText: and having prayed, they said, “You, LORD, who are knowing the heart of all, show which one You chose of these two,

1:26.sourceText: καὶ ἔδωκαν κλήρους αὐτοῖς, καὶ ἔπεσεν ὁ κλῆρος ἐπὶ Μαθθίαν, καὶ συνκατεψηφίσθη μετὰ τῶν ἕνδεκα ἀποστόλων.
